title: State of Mind: Learning and Evaluating World Models of Naturalistic Brain Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2611.28508v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Understanding naturalistic brain activity requires going beyond the stimulus alone, as external inputs continuously interact with an individual's evolving brain state. A world model captures such dynamics in a latent state by inferring it from neural observations, predicting stimulus-driven evolution, and updating with new observations. However, existing brain world models fail to maintain a persistent latent state over time, and standard metrics of neural prediction accuracy cannot tell whether a model tracks an individual's brain state or relies solely on the stimulus. To directly test state inference, prediction, and updating, we introduce BrainStateBench, which evaluates a model's latent state through a frozen linear probe on whole-cortex, movie-driven fMRI. Its State task tests whether a model captures trial-to-trial variability in an individual's responses to repeated stimuli, while Forecast and Updating evaluate future activity

translated_title: 心智状态：学习与评估自然主义脑动力学的世界模型
translated_abstract: 理解自然主义的大脑活动需要超越单纯的刺激本身，因为外部输入与个体不断演化的大脑状态持续相互作用。世界模型通过从神经观测中推断潜在状态、预测刺激驱动的演化并根据新观测进行更新，从而在潜在状态中捕捉这种动态。然而，现有的脑世界模型无法在时间上维持一个持续的潜在状态，而且标准的神经预测精度指标无法判断模型是在追踪个体的大脑状态，还是仅仅依赖刺激。为了直接检验状态推断、预测和更新能力，我们提出了BrainStateBench，它通过在全皮层、电影驱动的fMRI数据上使用冻结的线性探针来评估模型的潜在状态。其State任务测试模型是否捕捉了个体对重复刺激响应中的逐试次变异性，而Forecast和Updating任务则评估未来活动（的预测与状态更新能力）。
tldr: 该论文提出了BrainStateBench基准，通过在全皮层电影fMRI上使用冻结线性探针，评估脑世界模型推断、预测和更新潜在大脑状态的能力，从而区分模型是否真正追踪个体的脑状态而非仅依赖外部刺激。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces BrainStateBench, a benchmark that uses frozen linear probes on whole-cortex movie-driven fMRI to evaluate whether brain world models can truly infer, predict, and update an individual's latent brain state, rather than merely relying on the stimulus alone.
